laws.title: The City and the Field — the Cry-Out Rule and the Bride-Price Marriage
laws.kjv_text: If a damsel that is a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her; Then ye shall bring them both out unto the gate of that city, and ye shall stone them with stones that they die; the damsel, because she cried not, being in the city; and the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife... But if a man find a betrothed damsel in the field, and the man force her, and lie with her: then the man only that lay with her shall die: But unto the damsel thou shalt do nothing; there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death... For he found her in the field, and the betrothed damsel cried, and there was none to save her. If a man find a damsel that is a virgin, which is not betrothed, and lay hold on her, and lie with her, and they be found; Then the man that lay with her shall give unto the damsel's father fifty shekels of silver, and she shall be his wife; because he hath humbled her, he may not put her away all his days.
laws.summary: Three linked cases graded entirely by geography and evidence, not by consent: a betrothed woman assaulted in the city is presumed complicit and stoned alongside her attacker because a city-dweller could theoretically be heard; the same woman assaulted in an open field is presumed innocent, because no one could have heard her cry for help; and an unbetrothed virgin who is 'found' with a man must be married to him for life, at a fixed bride-price, with no right of divorce ever granted him.
laws.original_audience: Israelite legal authorities administering betrothal and virginity law in an agrarian society where 'the city' and 'the field' were genuinely distinct zones of expected safety and isolation.
laws.immediate_context: Part of the Deuteronomic sexual-purity code (Deut 22:13-30), which opens with a bride's virginity being litigated by physical tokens (22:13-21) and closes with incest law (22:30). This passage is the Torah's only attempt at a consent standard, and it is entirely circumstantial: the presumption of guilt or innocence turns on where the act occurred, never on anything the woman herself did or said.
laws.historical_context: The city/field distinction is a real, and in its own terms almost humane, forensic innovation for its era — it explicitly rejects 'she must have wanted it' as the default and instead reasons from opportunity to cry for help, arriving at 22:26's remarkable sentence: 'there is in the damsel no sin worthy of death... even so is this matter [as when a man rises against his neighbor and kills him]' — an explicit analogy to being the victim of violent assault, not a participant in it. But the rule's mechanics still make a woman's exculpation depend entirely on unwitnessed geography, and the closing case (22:28-29) treats an unmarried victim's future as a transaction owed to her father, resolved by permanent marriage to her attacker rather than any relief to her.
laws.penalty: City case: both parties stoned. Field case: the man alone dies; the woman is explicitly cleared, 'there is... no sin worthy of death.' Unbetrothed case: fifty shekels to the father and mandatory, permanent marriage, with the perpetual-marriage clause functioning as the woman's only stated 'remedy.'
laws.exceptions: The field case is itself the exception the passage carves out of a harsher default; nothing further modifies it in the immediate text.
nt_passages: John 8:3-11 — Jesus refuses to apply a comparable presumption of guilt to a woman 'taken in adultery,' regardless of city or field
Matthew 1:19 — Joseph, believing Mary pregnant by another, resolves to act 'not willing to make her a publick example' — a quiet reversal of the shaming logic this statute assumes

internal_contradictions.issue: The passage's own logic (22:26-27) explicitly clears a woman assaulted where no help could reach her — precisely the situation of a remote or isolated setting — yet institutions built on this same Code routinely process isolated-setting assault victims as complicit anyway, ignoring the one place their own inerrant text draws an unambiguous line in their favor.

The unbetrothed case's 'remedy' (22:28-29) is lifelong marriage to the assailant with no right of divorce ever granted him — framed as protection for the woman's economic future, it forecloses her own consent to marriage a second time, this time permanently, as the price of the first violation.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Family Purity Administration's founding text for adjudicating assault claims: the 'city or field' inquiry is preserved almost verbatim as the first question in any Title IV sexual-assault intake — was the location one where a cry for help could plausibly have been heard? A finding of 'field' (isolation) formally clears the victim of any presumption of complicity, exactly as the statute requires. In practice, re-education camps and holding facilities are consistently found, on inspection, to satisfy the 'field' standard — remote, unheard, no one to save her — which makes the FPA's own doctrine, honestly applied, an acquittal for every victim assaulted in state custody. It is not honestly applied. Custody cases are administratively routed instead through the sotah/jealousy framework (`num-005-011-jealousy-ordeal-sotah`) or reclassified as a purity matter arising from the original offense that led to her detention, so the geographic exculpation the state's own law guarantees her is never actually reached. The unbetrothed marriage remedy (22:28-29) survives as the **Restitution Marriage** option in Family Order law — rarely invoked, mostly by families seeking to avoid the shame of an unmarried pregnancy, and never available to a woman already in state custody, since the camp itself has no father to whom fifty shekels might be owed.
laws.constitutional_analogue: The closest biblical approach to a corroboration-based consent standard, and — read honestly — more protective of an isolated-setting victim than the regime that claims this text as inerrant law actually is; a real-world echo of jurisdictions where a victim's 'opportunity to resist or flee' still perversely shapes prosecutorial charging decisions.
scene_ideas: An FPA intake officer running the 'city or field' questionnaire on Laura's case, checking every box the statute requires for exculpation, and then watching a supervisor reclassify the file anyway.
A defense counsel reading Deuteronomy 22:26-27 aloud in full, slowly, in a room where everyone already knows it will change nothing.
A Restitution Marriage broker's office, quietly doing a brisk business in families who would rather marry a daughter to her assailant than have the assault on record at all.
satirical_uses: The regime's own foundational sexual-assault statute contains a clean, geography-based acquittal for exactly Laura's situation, and administers her case as though the verse does not exist — because the verse that would clear her was never the one anyone intended to enforce.
bureaucratic_uses: the administrative reclassification memo that moves a 'field'-cleared case into sotah/jealousy jurisdiction instead

laws.title: Put Away Leaven; Eat Unleavened Bread (the Purge)
laws.kjv_text: Seven days shall ye eat unleavened bread; even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses: for whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.
laws.summary: During the seven days of Unleavened Bread, all leaven must be purged from the house and only unleavened bread eaten; eating leavened bread means being 'cut off from Israel.'
laws.original_audience: Israel at the first Passover and every Passover after; the leaven purge memorializes the haste of the Exodus (no time for bread to rise).
laws.immediate_context: The Passover institution (Ex 12); the leaven ban runs the seven-day feast, with a household search for leaven that became a formal rite.
laws.historical_context: Leaven became a standing metaphor for corruption and pride (1 Cor 5:6-8, 'a little leaven leaveneth the whole lump'; Jesus's 'leaven of the Pharisees'). The household search for leaven (bedikat chametz) is one of the most domestic, intimate rituals in the tradition — a family, by candlelight, hunting crumbs.
laws.penalty: Being 'cut off from Israel' — the same karet exclusion as the uncircumcised.
laws.exceptions: None during the feast. Outside the holy week, leavened bread is ordinary and permitted.
nt_passages: 1 Corinthians 5:6-8 — 'purge out therefore the old leaven'; the feast spiritualized into moral purity
Luke 12:1 — 'beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy'
Matthew 13:33 — leaven as the kingdom (a rare positive), an inconvenient counter-image

internal_contradictions.issue: Leaven is 'cut off'-level corruption during the holy week yet the image of the kingdom itself in Matthew 13:33 — the same substance is damnation and the reign of God depending on the page.

laws.usofc_implementation: The keystone of the Bread Laws. During the holy weeks the Bureau of Daily Bread issues only government-milled unleavened flour; leaven, honey, herbs, and private sourdough starters are contraband (a 'symbol of impurity and disobedience'), and households undergo — or self-perform under threat of inspection — the Search for Leaven. Eating leavened bread in the holy week is a 'cutting off' offense: sanctity-score collapse, ration suspension, and, aggravated, re-education. The domestic candlelight search becomes a surveillance ritual: a family hunting its own crumbs while the Manna watches.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Sumptuary and dietary law enforced into the home; the household search is a warrantless inspection normalized as devotion.
scene_ideas: The father bakes his late wife's old cookies in Year 10 and is reported for the unleavened-week violation — the tenderest act in the play caught by the harshest, smallest law. (This is the play's climax; the cookies and the smuggled letters are found together.)
The family's annual Search for Leaven, once warm, now performed knowing a neighbor or a child may report what the candle finds.
A black-market sourdough starter passed hand to hand like samizdat.
satirical_uses: A regime that calls leaven the image of the kingdom of God for fifty-one weeks makes eating it a 'cutting off' crime for one.

laws.title: Gather Daily, Leave None Till Morning (the Manna Rule)
laws.kjv_text: And Moses said, Let no man leave of it till the morning. Notwithstanding they hearkened not unto Moses; but some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and stank: and Moses was wroth with them.
laws.summary: The manna in the wilderness had to be gathered daily and eaten the same day; what was hoarded 'bred worms and stank.' A law of daily dependence and against accumulation.
laws.original_audience: Israel in the wilderness, fed by daily manna and taught daily reliance on God (with a double portion before the sabbath).
laws.immediate_context: Exodus 16, the manna narrative; the rule teaches dependence and prefigures 'give us this day our daily bread.' A double portion is provided for the sabbath — the one permitted 'hoard.'
laws.historical_context: The manna economy is the Bible's anti-accumulation parable: enough for today, nothing stored, no advantage to the strong gatherer ('he that gathered much had nothing over,' 16:18) — which Paul cites for economic equality (2 Cor 8:15). It is the scriptural opposite of a market in grain.
laws.penalty: The hoarded portion spoils — 'bred worms, and stank.' The punishment is built into the bread.
laws.exceptions: The sabbath double portion (Ex 16:22-26), which did not spoil — the one sanctioned store.
nt_passages: Matthew 6:11 — 'Give us this day our daily bread'
2 Corinthians 8:15 — 'he that had gathered much had nothing over,' cited for equality
Luke 12:16-21 — the rich fool who built bigger barns to hoard

internal_contradictions.issue: The manna rule is a divine argument *against* accumulation and *for* equal daily provision (2 Cor 8:15) — which the USOC inverts into a rationing-and-scarcity control while its prosperity clergy build exactly the bigger barns Luke 12 condemns.

laws.usofc_implementation: The scriptural charter of the ration system. The Bureau of Daily Bread issues bread against the Manna platform on a same-day basis: rations must be collected and consumed the day they are issued (the anti-hoarding rule, 'lest it breed worms'), and unused allocation simply lapses — you cannot save, stockpile, or transfer. Tied to it is the 'Idleness Loaf' policy (only registered workers draw a full ration; cf. 2 Thess 3:10) and a holy-week suspension. A humane parable of daily provision becomes an instrument of daily dependence: no citizen can accumulate enough to be independent of the state for even a week — except the wealthy, whose 'sabbath double portion' exemptions never lapse.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Rationing law fused with anti-hoarding decree; the same-day-lapse mechanic is a food-based social-credit throttle with no secular equivalent outside siege or famine command economies.
scene_ideas: The family's ration lapses because the mother was detained past sundown collecting it — a day's hunger as a bureaucratic side effect.
A black market in 'yesterday's bread' — the smell of the spoiled hoard as the smell of resistance.
The wealthy family's pantry, full and lawful under a 'sabbath double portion' exemption, glimpsed in Act 1 and understood only in Act 2.
satirical_uses: A parable against hoarding, run by a clergy that hoards, enforced against a people who cannot — 'daily bread' as a leash.
bureaucratic_uses: same-day ration issuance and lapse (the Manna platform)
sabbath double-portion exemptions for high tiers

laws.title: No Other Gods
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt have no other gods before me.
laws.summary: The first commandment: exclusive allegiance to YHWH. No rival deities may be acknowledged, worshipped, or ranked alongside him.
laws.original_audience: The assembled Israelites at Mount Sinai, newly delivered from Egypt, constituted as a covenant people.
laws.immediate_context: Opening of the Decalogue (Ex 20:1-17), delivered directly by God amid thunder and smoke; the preamble (v.2) grounds the demand in the Exodus deliverance.
laws.historical_context: Formally parallels Hittite suzerainty treaties: a great king's exclusive-loyalty clause following a historical prologue. The wording ('before me') presumes other gods exist to be rejected — monolatry rather than philosophical monotheism, which develops later (cf. Deutero-Isaiah).
laws.penalty: None stated here; elsewhere death (Ex 22:20, Deut 13:6-10) and covenant curses.
laws.exceptions: None.
nt_passages: Matthew 4:10 — Jesus cites exclusive worship against Satan
Mark 12:29-30 — the Shema as the greatest commandment
1 Corinthians 8:5-6 — 'gods many, and lords many' but one God
Acts 17:22-31 — Paul negotiates pluralism in Athens without a death penalty

internal_contradictions.issue: How many gods are there? Exclusive monotheism (Deut 4:35, Isa 44:6) vs. passages presuming plural gods (Gen 1:26, Ex 12:12, Ps 82).

laws.usofc_implementation: Article I of the Covenant Amendment. Operationalized as the Exclusive Allegiance Registry: every citizen files an annual Declaration of Sole Worship; membership in any non-covenanted religious body is a first-degree Covenant felony. Foreign embassies negotiate 'diplomatic worship exemptions.'
laws.constitutional_analogue: Directly annuls the First Amendment's Establishment and Free Exercise Clauses; the founding repeal on which the entire USofC rests.
scene_ideas: A Hindu-American family's annual 'allegiance audit,' their home shrine hidden behind a false wall of Covenant-approved decor.
An OIP hearing debating whether a yoga studio's sun salutation constitutes 'having' another god.
The President privately consults an astrologer; the transcript becomes the season's blackmail engine.
satirical_uses: The state that enforces 'no other gods' functionally worships itself — the OIP's seal appears in more homes than any cross.
Mammon is conspicuously absent from the enforcement priorities.
bureaucratic_uses: Annual Declaration of Sole Worship (Form W-1)
Exclusive Allegiance Registry with tiered suspicion scores

laws.title: No Graven Images
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image, or any likeness of any thing that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.
laws.summary: Prohibits manufacturing carved cult images — read literally, any likeness of anything in sky, earth, or sea.
laws.original_audience: Israelites at Sinai; aimed at the image-saturated cults of Egypt and Canaan they knew.
laws.immediate_context: Second commandment; paired with v.5's ban on venerating images. The golden calf episode (Ex 32) follows within weeks of narrative time.
laws.historical_context: Aniconism was rare and striking in the ancient Near East, where a cult statue was the god's presence in the temple. Israel's imageless worship became its defining religious marker. Yet the tabernacle itself commands cherubim images (Ex 25:18), so the working line was always 'no images for worship,' not 'no images.'
laws.penalty: None stated in the verse; idolaters elsewhere face death (Deut 27:15 curses the image-maker).
laws.exceptions: God commands images elsewhere: cherubim (Ex 25:18), the bronze serpent (Num 21:8), lions and oxen in Solomon's temple (1 Kings 7:25,29).
nt_passages: John 3:14 — Jesus compares himself to the bronze serpent image
Acts 17:29 — the Godhead is not like gold or stone
Colossians 1:15 — Christ as the 'image of the invisible God' complicates aniconism
Romans 1:23 — images as the root of pagan decline

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it OK to make images? This total ban vs. God commanding cherubim, the bronze serpent, and temple statuary.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Graven Images Act. The OIP Iconoclasm Division licenses all representational art; 'devotional risk' is scored by subject, scale, and placement. Photography survived by a landmark ruling that a photograph is 'light, not graving.' Statues of USofC founders are exempted as 'civic memorials, not likenesses' — the most litigated sentence in the Code.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Collides with First Amendment free expression; functionally a national art-censorship regime.
scene_ideas: An Iconoclasm Division inspector and a museum curator negotiating which Renaissance paintings get the drape.
A child's science-fair diorama of the solar system seized as 'likeness of things in heaven above.'
Underground portrait painters working from memory so no 'likeness' technically exists.
satirical_uses: The regime that bans likenesses plasters the President's face on every licensing form — ruled 'a seal, not an image.'
bureaucratic_uses: Representational Art License with devotional-risk scoring
Form IC-2: Application to Depict a Created Thing
The Drape Registry for museum loans

laws.title: No Bowing to or Serving Images; Transgenerational Punishment
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the LORD thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me; And shewing mercy unto thousands of them that love me, and keep my commandments.
laws.summary: Forbids venerating or serving images, and attaches a sanction principle: guilt runs downstream three to four generations; loyalty earns mercy to thousands.
laws.original_audience: Israelites at Sinai, organized in multigenerational households where a patriarch's cult choice bound the family.
laws.immediate_context: Completes the image prohibition of v.4 and states the covenant's incentive structure.
laws.historical_context: Collective and transgenerational liability was normal in ancient Near Eastern law (Hammurabi punishes a builder's son for the builder's fault). Ezekiel 18 later repudiates the principle within the Bible itself — a rare visible instance of biblical law reforming biblical law.
laws.penalty: Divine sanction: iniquity 'visited' on descendants to the third and fourth generation.
laws.exceptions: Deuteronomy 24:16 forbids human courts from doing exactly what this verse says God does.
nt_passages: John 9:2-3 — 'who did sin, this man, or his parents?' Jesus rejects the inherited-guilt frame
Romans 5:12-19 — inherited Adamic guilt as the doctrine's cosmic version

internal_contradictions.issue: Are we punished for the sins of others? This verse vs. Ezekiel 18:20 and Deuteronomy 24:16 ('every man shall be put to death for his own sin').

laws.usofc_implementation: The Generational Standing system: convictions for Covenant felonies attach a 'lineage flag' to descendants for four generations — barring federal employment, clergy licensing, and Council eligibility. Officially 'not punishment, merely prudence.' Mercy-to-thousands is implemented as hereditary honor status for founding families.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Violates the Constitution's Corruption of Blood clause (Art. III §3) and Fifth/Fourteenth Amendment due process; a hereditary caste system by database.
scene_ideas: A brilliant candidate for the Council discovers her great-grandfather's sealed idolatry conviction the week of her confirmation.
A DOR clerk whose entire job is adjudicating whether a fourth generation has 'elapsed' — counting from conviction, birth, or conception is a live circuit split.
Lineage-flag laundering: marrying into a mercy-to-thousands family scrubs the record.
satirical_uses: The state cites Ezekiel 18 to deny it punishes children for parents, while the lineage database does precisely that — 'the flag is administrative, not penal.'
bureaucratic_uses: Generational Standing Certificate required for federal hiring
Lineage-flag appeals with a four-generation actuarial table
Hereditary honor rolls for 'thousands of them that love me'

laws.title: The Name Not in Vain
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not take the name of the LORD thy God in vain; for the LORD will not hold him guiltless that taketh his name in vain.
laws.summary: Forbids empty, deceitful, or profane use of God's name — in its original setting, chiefly false oaths sworn by YHWH.
laws.original_audience: Israelites for whom oaths by the divine name were the backbone of contracts, testimony, and treaties.
laws.immediate_context: Third commandment; guards the covenant name revealed in Ex 3:14 and invoked in every legal proceeding.
laws.historical_context: In a world without notaries, the divine name was the enforcement mechanism of commerce: swearing falsely 'in the name' weaponized the god against the innocent party. Later Jewish practice fenced the law by never pronouncing the Name at all. Leviticus 24:16 sets stoning for blaspheming the Name.
laws.penalty: 'The LORD will not hold him guiltless' — divine sanction; blasphemy earns death by stoning in Lev 24:16.
laws.exceptions: Lawful oaths in God's name are commanded, not merely permitted (Deut 6:13, 10:20).
nt_passages: Matthew 5:33-37 — Jesus forbids oaths entirely: 'Swear not at all'
James 5:12 — repeats the total oath ban
Matthew 26:63-64 — Jesus answers under oath before the high priest

internal_contradictions.issue: Deuteronomy commands swearing by God's name; Jesus and James forbid all swearing — the USofC courtroom oath is scripturally impossible either way.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Sacred Speech Act. The SSC maintains the Register of Permitted Exclamations; broadcast media run a two-second Name-delay. Perjury on a Covenant oath is prosecuted as blasphemy, not mere false statement. The Matthew 5 'swear not at all' problem was resolved by CSC ruling: courtroom oaths are 'covenant affirmations,' not swearing.
laws.constitutional_analogue: A national blasphemy law; annuls First Amendment speech protection and the Art. VI option to affirm rather than swear.
scene_ideas: A live-broadcast engineer's finger hovering over the Name-delay button during a senator's unraveling speech.
An SSC linguist testifying whether 'gosh' is a euphemistic misdemeanor or protected folk speech.
A Quaker-descended defendant citing Matthew 5:34 to refuse the oath — and being charged under the very statute the oath serves.
satirical_uses: The state takes the Name in vain constantly — printing it on currency, campaign ads, and missile casings — because official use is by definition not 'vain.'
bureaucratic_uses: Register of Permitted Exclamations, updated quarterly
Blasphemy incident reports (Form SSC-7) with severity codes

laws.title: Remember the Sabbath
laws.kjv_text: Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work: But the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates.
laws.summary: Mandates a weekly work stoppage for the whole household economy — children, servants, livestock, and resident foreigners included — grounded in God's rest after creation.
laws.original_audience: Israelite householders, who controlled whether dependents and animals rested.
laws.immediate_context: Fourth commandment, the hinge between duties to God and duties to neighbor; the longest commandment, with the only creation-based rationale (Deut 5:15 gives a different one — the Exodus).
laws.historical_context: A seven-day rest cycle detached from lunar phases is without clear ancient Near Eastern parallel and became Israel's signature institution. Numbers 15:32-36 shows enforcement: a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath is stoned. The commandment is notably humane toward labor and notably lethal toward violators.
laws.penalty: Death (Ex 31:14-15, Numbers 15:32-36); here, none stated.
laws.exceptions: Priestly temple labor proceeds (Matt 12:5); later rabbinic principle that saving life overrides the Sabbath; Jesus adds healing and need (Mark 2:23-28).
nt_passages: Mark 2:27 — 'The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath'
Matthew 12:1-14 — Jesus defends Sabbath healing and gleaning
Colossians 2:16 — let no man judge you regarding sabbaths
Romans 14:5 — every day alike, let each be persuaded
Hebrews 4:9 — sabbath rest spiritualized

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it necessary to keep the Sabbath? Capital enforcement (Ex 31:14) vs. Colossians 2:16 and Romans 14:5 releasing believers from sabbath judgment.
Which day? The USofC enforces Sunday, but the commandment's seventh day is Saturday — the regime criminalizes the calendar it inherited.

laws.usofc_implementation: The National Sabbath Act: total commercial shutdown Saturday sundown to Sunday sundown ('the Bridged Sabbath,' a denominational compromise that satisfied no one). The BSO issues Sabbath Exemption Licenses by criticality tier — hospitals Tier 1, power grid Tier 2, professional football Tier 3 after the largest lobbying campaign in USofC history. Household compliance is presumed but neighbor-reportable.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Blue laws taken to their limit; McGowan v. Maryland (1961) upheld Sunday closing on secular grounds — the USofC deleted the secular fig leaf.
scene_ideas: An ER admitting clerk deciding at 11:58 p.m. whether an injury is 'life-threatening' or 'Monday-treatable.'
A BSO inspector timing a farmer's cows to determine whether the milking robot constitutes the cattle working.
The annual Exemption License auction — officially an 'ordered stewardship allocation' — where criticality tiers are openly bought.
satirical_uses: The football exemption: the regime found stoning a stick-gatherer scriptural but Sunday kickoff non-negotiable.
Enforcement agents work every Sabbath, covered by a standing auto-renewed exemption no one has re-read in years.
bureaucratic_uses: Sabbath Exemption License with criticality tiers and renewal fees
The Bridged Sabbath interdenominational treaty text

laws.title: Honor Father and Mother
laws.kjv_text: Honour thy father and thy mother: that thy days may be long upon the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee.
laws.summary: Positive duty of honor toward both parents, with a stated reward: long tenure in the land. The only commandment with an attached promise.
laws.original_audience: Primarily adult Israelites responsible for aging parents' maintenance, not small children being told to obey.
laws.immediate_context: Fifth commandment, opening the second tablet's social duties; enforced elsewhere by capital statutes against striking or cursing parents (Ex 21:15,17).
laws.historical_context: In a society without pensions, 'honor' meant material support of the old. Wisdom literature and ANE instruction texts (e.g., Egyptian Instruction of Any) carry the same duty. Jesus attacks the corban loophole by which dedicated funds escaped the obligation (Mark 7:9-13).
laws.penalty: None here (reward stated instead); striking or cursing a parent is death (Ex 21:15,17); the incorrigible son is stoned (Deut 21:18-21).
laws.exceptions: Jesus repeatedly relativizes family duty toward himself (Matt 10:35-37, Luke 14:26).
nt_passages: Ephesians 6:1-3 — Paul quotes it as 'the first commandment with promise'
Mark 7:9-13 — Jesus condemns the corban loophole
Matthew 10:35-37 — 'he that loveth father or mother more than me is not worthy of me'
Luke 14:26 — 'if any man... hate not his father, and mother... he cannot be my disciple'

internal_contradictions.issue: How should parents be treated? Honor them (here) vs. Jesus requiring disciples to 'hate' father and mother.
Is it OK to call your father 'father'? Matthew 23:9 says call no man father — awkward for the commandment's wording.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Filial Piety Act: adult children file annual Parental Maintenance Statements; support is payroll-deducted like a second social security aimed backward. Public dishonor of a parent (defined by regulation, 40 pages) is a civil infraction ladder that tops out, theoretically, at the Incorrigibility Statute — never yet invoked, always available.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Filial responsibility laws exist in ~30 US states, rarely enforced; the USofC enforces them universally and criminally.
scene_ideas: An estranged daughter's maintenance garnishment funding the abusive father she fled.
A DFO mediator processing a corban-style trust — funds 'dedicated to the Church' to starve out a parent — with Mark 7 read aloud by opposing counsel.
The first prosecutor to actually file under the Incorrigibility Statute becoming a national crisis.
satirical_uses: The promise clause is administered literally: verified honorers receive an actuarial bonus called Longevity Credit, paid, with no irony, from the estates of the dishonoring.
bureaucratic_uses: Dishonor infraction schedule with point system

laws.title: Thou Shalt Not Kill
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not kill.
laws.summary: Prohibits unlawful killing. The Hebrew verb (ratsach) targets murder and manslaughter of persons within the community, not all killing — war, execution, and animal slaughter proceed under other statutes.
laws.original_audience: Israelite covenant community; the ban protects members from each other, not enemies from Israel.
laws.immediate_context: Sixth commandment; the Covenant Code immediately elaborates it into degrees — murder, manslaughter, refuge (Ex 21:12-14).
laws.historical_context: Homicide law is universal in ANE codes; Israel's distinctives are refusal of monetary ransom for murder (Num 35:31, contrast Hammurabi's composition payments) and the blood-pollution theology: unavenged blood defiles the land itself (Num 35:33).
laws.penalty: Death for murder (Ex 21:12); exile to refuge for manslaughter (Num 35).
laws.exceptions: Capital punishment commanded (Ex 21:12ff), war commanded (Deut 20), and divinely ordered killings throughout the conquest narratives.
nt_passages: Matthew 5:21-22 — Jesus extends the ban to anger and contempt
Matthew 26:52 — 'they that take the sword shall perish with the sword'
Romans 13:4 — the ruler 'beareth not the sword in vain', the state's favorite verse
1 John 3:15 — hatred as murder

internal_contradictions.issue: To kill or not to kill: the commandment vs. God repeatedly commanding killings (1 Sam 15:3, Deut 7:2) — the SAB's central exhibit.

laws.usofc_implementation: Title IV's cornerstone. The USofC preserves the ratsach reading loudly: murder is capital, but state executions, sanctioned war, and 'covenant defense' are definitionally not killing. Per Numbers 35:31, plea-bargaining a murder charge to a fine is scripturally barred — the one place the regime's courts are genuinely, terrifyingly incorruptible.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Ordinary homicide law, minus Eighth Amendment proportionality and with mandatory capital sentencing.
scene_ideas: A defense attorney's entire practice: relitigating the Hebrew verb, one preposition at a time.
An execution chamber with Matthew 5:21 stenciled over the door by a chaplain who has stopped sleeping.
A prosecutor who cannot offer the plea deal both families are begging for, because Numbers 35:31 forbids ransom.
satirical_uses: The commandment appears on the Department of War's letterhead, untranslated, in Hebrew — so no one can be sure it applies.
bureaucratic_uses: Homicide classification worksheet: murder / manslaughter / covenant defense / sanctioned act
Blood-pollution land audits after unsolved killings (Deut 21:1-9 heifer procedure, still on the books)

laws.title: No Adultery
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not commit adultery.
laws.summary: Prohibits adultery — in its original legal sense, intercourse with another man's wife or betrothed; a property-and-paternity offense against the husband.
laws.original_audience: Israelite men and married/betrothed women; a married man's relations with an unattached woman fell under different, lesser rules.
laws.immediate_context: Seventh commandment; Lev 20:10 and Deut 22:22 supply the death penalty for both parties.
laws.historical_context: ANE codes (Hammurabi 129, Middle Assyrian 13-16) treat adultery similarly but let the husband pardon; biblical law makes it an offense against God that the husband cannot waive. The asymmetry — defined around the woman's status, not the man's — is the law's structural misogyny.
laws.penalty: Death for both parties (Leviticus 20:10, Deuteronomy 22:22).
laws.exceptions: Polygamy and concubinage are lawful for men throughout the Old Testament; the double standard is the exception built in.
nt_passages: Matthew 5:27-28 — Jesus extends adultery to the lustful look
John 8:3-11 — Jesus declines to stone the adulteress: 'he that is without sin'
Matthew 19:9 — remarriage after divorce as adultery
Hebrews 13:4 — 'whoremongers and adulterers God will judge'

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it wrong to commit adultery? The command vs. narratives where God gives David his master's wives (2 Sam 12:8) and patriarchal polygamy passes without censure.
John 8 (the regime's least favorite pericope) shows Jesus nullifying the prescribed stoning — CSC classifies the passage as 'textually disputed,' which is, inconveniently, true.

laws.usofc_implementation: Adultery is a Covenant felony prosecuted by the FPA; the two-witness rule makes conviction nearly impossible, so the real instrument is the Numbers 5 jealousy ordeal, revived as a 'voluntary marital integrity screening' whose refusal is admissible. Capital in statute, commuted in practice to Marriage Dissolution with Prejudice — except in election years.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Adultery was criminal in many states into the 20th century; Lawrence v. Texas (2003) ended morals policing of private consensual conduct — repealed here.
scene_ideas: A jealousy-ordeal administration: holy water, floor dust from the Covenant Court, a wife who knows the chemistry is fake and the social verdict is not.
Two co-workers who witnessed an affair deciding whether to become the two witnesses — and learning what corroboration pays.
An FPA prosecutor quietly shelving a case against a Council member's son while the John 8 mural across the street undergoes 'restoration.'
satirical_uses: Matthew 5:28 makes every citizen guilty; the FPA's founding memo concedes this and recommends 'enforcement at scale is neither possible nor desirable — selectivity is the program.'

laws.title: No Stealing
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not steal.
laws.summary: Prohibits theft of property (and, on one ancient reading, theft of persons — kidnapping, cf. Ex 21:16).
laws.original_audience: Israelite community of smallholders whose animals and tools were survival capital.
laws.immediate_context: Eighth commandment; the Covenant Code's restitution schedule (Ex 22:1-4) supplies the remedies.
laws.historical_context: Where Hammurabi punishes some theft with death (CH 6-10), biblical law is strikingly non-capital about property: thieves pay multiples (double to fivefold restitution), and only manstealing is capital. Property crime never outranks persons — a fact the USofC finds continually inconvenient.
laws.penalty: Restitution: double for possession, four sheep or five oxen for slaughtered/sold animals (Ex 22:1,4); sold into servitude if unable to pay (Ex 22:3).
laws.exceptions: Eating from a neighbor's standing field or vineyard on the spot is lawful (Deut 23:24-25); gleaning rights (Lev 19:9-10) make some 'taking' a right of the poor.
nt_passages: Ephesians 4:28 — 'let him that stole steal no more: but rather let him labour'
Luke 19:8 — Zacchaeus's fourfold restitution as the Exodus schedule internalized
Acts 4:32-35 — the Jerusalem church holding all things common

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it wrong to steal? The command vs. the Israelites 'borrowing' and despoiling the Egyptians at God's instruction (Ex 3:22, 12:35-36).

laws.usofc_implementation: Theft is handled by the Restitution Administration on the biblical multiplier schedule — no prison for property crime, a genuinely popular reform. Judgment debtors who cannot pay enter covenant labor (see exo-021-002). Gleaning and field-eating rights are codified but hedged: exercising them requires a Gleaner's Card, and the queue for the card is the point.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Replaces incarceration-based larceny law with restitution and debt servitude; collides with the Thirteenth Amendment's exception clause, which the USofC quotes with enthusiasm.
scene_ideas: An RA hearing computing whether a stolen 3D printer is an 'ox' (fivefold, productive capital) or a 'sheep' (fourfold) — the multiplier bar exam question.
A supermarket's legal team arguing shelf-grazing customers are exercising Deut 23:24 field-eating rights.
A Gleaner's Card office that opens for two hours on alternating Tuesdays.
satirical_uses: The despoiling-of-Egypt precedent is taught in USofC law schools as 'the eminent domain of the righteous.'

laws.title: No False Witness
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.
laws.summary: Prohibits perjured testimony against a member of the community; the integrity clause of a legal system that runs entirely on witnesses.
laws.original_audience: Israelites, whose courts had no forensics — two or three witnesses were the whole evidentiary apparatus (Deut 19:15).
laws.immediate_context: Ninth commandment; Deut 19:16-21 adds the enforcement: a proven false witness suffers whatever penalty he sought for the accused.
laws.historical_context: Hammurabi opens his code (CH 1-4) the same way: false capital accusation is itself capital. When testimony is the only evidence, perjury is the system's single point of failure — both codes know it.
laws.penalty: Talionic: 'then shall ye do unto him, as he had thought to have done unto his brother' (Deut 19:19) — up to death for false capital testimony.
laws.exceptions: None. (Narratively, God sends a lying spirit in 1 Kings 22:22 — the awkward footnote.)
nt_passages: Matthew 26:59-61 — false witnesses sought against Jesus
Acts 6:11-13 — false witnesses against Stephen
Matthew 18:16 — Jesus imports the two-witness rule into church discipline

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God countenance deception? The absolute ban vs. God sending a lying spirit (1 Kings 22:22) and rewarding the Hebrew midwives' lie (Ex 1:19-20).

laws.usofc_implementation: The load-bearing wall of USofC justice. Because Deut 19:15 requires two witnesses for any conviction, a professional Certified Witness industry emerged — licensed, bonded, and traded. Proven perjury triggers the mirror penalty in full, including capital. The Naboth scenario (a rigged two-witness frame) is the regime's signature abuse and its official nightmare.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Perjury statutes plus the Confrontation Clause — but with a two-witness sufficiency rule the US Constitution reserves for treason alone (Art. III §3).
scene_ideas: A Certified Witness who has 'independently observed' forty crimes this fiscal year, testifying with the serenity of a notary.
The mirror-penalty execution of a false witness, attended by the man he almost hanged.
Two strangers who actually did see the crime, discovering the defense will impeach them for lacking witness licenses.
satirical_uses: The witness exchange has a ticker: corroboration futures rise every election season.

laws.title: No Coveting
laws.kjv_text: Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour's wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour's.
laws.summary: Prohibits desiring what belongs to a neighbor — house, wife, servants, livestock. The Decalogue's only regulation of a mental state; also its plainest inventory of persons as property.
laws.original_audience: Israelite householders; the 'neighbour' is a fellow covenant member, and the wife is listed among his assets.
laws.immediate_context: Tenth commandment, closing the Decalogue by moving from act to appetite — the root of theft, adultery, and murder in one verse.
laws.historical_context: Unique among ANE laws in criminalizing desire itself; no court could try it, which is precisely the point — it hands enforcement to conscience (or, in a theocracy, to whoever claims to audit conscience). The wife's placement between house and servants is Exhibit A for the property-status of women; Deuteronomy 5:21 pointedly re-orders to put her first and separate.
laws.penalty: None stated; unenforceable by human courts by design.
laws.exceptions: None.
cross_references: Joshua 7:21 (Achan: 'I coveted them, and took them')
nt_passages: Romans 7:7 — Paul says this commandment taught him what sin is
Luke 12:15 — 'beware of covetousness'
Colossians 3:5 — covetousness 'is idolatry'
James 1:14-15 — desire conceiving sin conceiving death

internal_contradictions.issue: Is it OK to covet? The ban vs. Paul's 'covet earnestly the best gifts' (1 Cor 12:31) — same Greek verb in the Septuagint's register.
Does God approve of slavery? The verse lists servants as covetable property, presupposing the institution.

laws.usofc_implementation: Unprosecutable, therefore perfect: the Covetousness Statute is the regime's universal pretext. Compliance runs through the NDS's Weekly Confession Assemblies, where citizens self-report desires; the confessions are logged. Advertising is regulated as 'incitement to covet,' giving the state a licensing chokehold on all marketing — the quietest, most total power in the Code.
laws.constitutional_analogue: A pure thought-crime statute; the First Amendment and the entire liberal distinction between act and belief are its casualties. Its advertising arm inverts commercial speech doctrine.
scene_ideas: A confession assembly where a man admits coveting his neighbor's Sabbath Exemption License — and the log entry follows him for a decade.
An ad agency's Compliance Poet, whose job is selling a truck without inducing desire for the truck.
A detective who closes cases by pulling covetousness logs: everyone has confessed to wanting something someone else lost.
satirical_uses: The state's own propaganda organ runs recruitment ads promising 'the life your neighbor has' — cleared by a ruling that inciting covetousness toward the state is devotion.

laws.title: No Gods of Silver or Gold
laws.kjv_text: Ye shall not make with me gods of silver, neither shall ye make unto you gods of gold.
laws.summary: Restates the image ban with specificity: no manufacturing deities from precious metals, even as companions ('with me') to YHWH's worship.
laws.original_audience: Israel via Moses, immediately after the Decalogue's public delivery; the golden calf (Ex 32) will violate it exactly.
laws.immediate_context: Opens the 'Book of the Covenant' (Ex 20:22-23:33), the oldest law collection in the Bible; bridges the Decalogue to the altar law.
laws.historical_context: Precious-metal cult statues were temple treasury and god at once; melting the calf and making Israel drink it (Ex 32:20) follows an attested ANE pattern for annihilating a god. The 'with me' clause targets syncretism — adding gods alongside, not just replacing.
laws.penalty: None stated; the calf episode answers with plague and sword (Ex 32:27-28,35).
laws.exceptions: The tabernacle is nonetheless furnished with gold cherubim and gold everything (Ex 25) — sanctioned images in the sanctuary the law protects.
nt_passages: Acts 17:29 — the Godhead is not like gold or silver
1 Peter 1:18 — redeemed not with silver and gold
Revelation 9:20 — idols of gold as end-times furniture

internal_contradictions.issue: Who gave the law to Moses? God directly (here), vs. angels (Gal 3:19, Acts 7:53, Heb 2:2).

laws.usofc_implementation: Implemented as the Precious Metals Devotional Use Act: bullion ownership above a threshold requires an OIP affidavit that the metal is 'inert' (non-devotional). Gold religious statuary is contraband; gold on state regalia is 'ornament, not god.' The statute's real function is asset surveillance wearing a mitre.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Free exercise casualty like the image ban; its asset-registry mechanics echo Executive Order 6102's gold confiscation, re-theologized.
scene_ideas: An OIP audit of a jeweler's back room: which crucifixes are 'ornament' and which are 'god' turns on the invoice wording.
A survivalist's gold coins seized as 'potential deities in specie.'
satirical_uses: The Federal Reserve of Christ keeps the national gold in a vault nicknamed, by everyone, the Calf.

laws.title: Altar of Earth; Sacrifice Where the Name Is Recorded
laws.kjv_text: An altar of earth thou shalt make unto me, and shalt sacrifice thereon thy burnt offerings, and thy peace offerings, thy sheep, and thine oxen: in all places where I record my name I will come unto thee, and I will bless thee.
laws.summary: Prescribes simple earthen altars for burnt and peace offerings, valid at every place God 'records his name' — a decentralized, multi-site sacrificial system.
laws.original_audience: Israelite worshippers pre-temple, sacrificing wherever the divine name was memorialized.
laws.immediate_context: First cultic statute of the Covenant Code, immediately following the Decalogue.
laws.historical_context: This 'altar law' authorizes many altars; Deuteronomy 12 later demands one central sanctuary and the destruction of all other sites — the classic evidence (since Wellhausen) that Israel's law codes come from different eras with different cult politics. Earth and unhewn stone reject Canaanite high-place masonry and, perhaps, ostentation itself.
laws.penalty: None stated.
laws.exceptions: Superseded (or contradicted) by Deuteronomy 12's central-sanctuary requirement.
nt_passages: John 4:20-24 — worship neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem, but in spirit and truth
Hebrews 13:10 — 'we have an altar' spiritualizing the institution
Matthew 5:23-24 — leave thy gift before the altar; be reconciled first

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God desire animal sacrifices? Commanded here vs. 'I desired mercy, and not sacrifice' (Hos 6:6) and Jeremiah 7:22 denying the command was ever given.
Did God command burnt offerings? Jeremiah 7:22 says no; this verse says yes.
Many altars (here) vs. one central sanctuary only (Deut 12) — two incompatible cult constitutions in one canon.

laws.usofc_implementation: The USofC does not practice animal sacrifice (CSC ruling: 'fulfilled in Christ,' citing Hebrews) — but the altar law survives as the Licensed Assembly Site regime: worship is lawful only at locations where the Name is 'recorded,' i.e., registered with the DOW. An unregistered prayer meeting is an unlicensed altar.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Assembly and worship licensing — the inverse of the First Amendment's assembly clause.
scene_ideas: A house church debating whether saying grace at dinner with guests constitutes an 'assembly' requiring site registration.
The DOW's Name Registry office, where a clerical error can deconsecrate a cathedral overnight.
satirical_uses: The one sacrifice the state retained is the licensing fee.

laws.title: No Hewn Stone Altars
laws.kjv_text: And if thou wilt make me an altar of stone, thou shalt not build it of hewn stone: for if thou lift up thy tool upon it, thou hast polluted it.
laws.summary: Stone altars must be of uncut fieldstone; applying a tool pollutes the altar.
laws.original_audience: Israelite altar-builders.
laws.immediate_context: Continues the altar law of v.24; Joshua obeys it exactly at Mount Ebal (Josh 8:31).
laws.historical_context: Possibly anti-Canaanite (dressed-stone high places), possibly an iron-taboo (cf. Deut 27:5 'lift up no iron tool'), possibly a theology of the unmanufactured: God's altar must not be human artifice. Solomon's temple, built of elaborately hewn stone, keeps the letter by pre-cutting off-site (1 Kings 6:7) — the Bible's first regulatory workaround.
laws.penalty: The altar is 'polluted' — ritually void.
laws.exceptions: The 1 Kings 6:7 off-site-fabrication workaround.
nt_passages: Mark 14:58 — 'temple made without hands' as the category's afterlife
Acts 7:48 — the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands
laws.usofc_implementation: Enforced literally for the ceremonial Gate Rooms of Covenant courthouses: their altar-tables must be uncut fieldstone, certified tool-free. A niche industry of 'providentially shaped stone' brokers sells suspiciously convenient boulders with notarized no-tool provenance.
laws.constitutional_analogue: None; closest analogue is historic-preservation materials law, weaponized.
scene_ideas: A forensic masonry hearing: microscopy slides projected in court to prove a chisel touched the courthouse altar in 1987, voiding every oath sworn on it since.
The 'convenient boulder' broker showing a client the quarry he definitely doesn't own.
satirical_uses: Off-site fabrication (1 Kings 6:7) is precedent: the whole regime runs on cutting the stone where God isn't looking.

laws.title: No Steps Up to the Altar
laws.kjv_text: Neither shalt thou go up by steps unto mine altar, that thy nakedness be not discovered thereon.
laws.summary: Altars may not be approached by steps, lest the officiant's genitals be exposed beneath his robe while climbing.
laws.original_audience: Altar officiants (pre-Aaronic; later priests get mandatory linen breeches instead, Ex 28:42).
laws.immediate_context: Closes the altar law and the chapter; modesty before God extends to architecture.
laws.historical_context: Ritual nudity was a feature of some ANE cults; Israel legislates against even accidental exposure. The priestly solution evolves: Ex 28:42 mandates underwear, after which Ezekiel's temple vision happily includes altar steps (Ezek 43:17) — a visible dialogue between statute and workaround.
laws.penalty: None stated; for priests, wrongful exposure at the altar risks death (Ex 28:43).
laws.exceptions: Effectively repealed by the breeches mandate (Ex 28:42-43); Ezekiel 43:17 shows a stepped altar.
nt_passages: No direct NT engagement; general modesty texts (1 Timothy 2:9) are the nearest register.

internal_contradictions.issue: No steps (here) vs. Ezekiel's altar with steps (Ezek 43:17) — resolved historically by the breeches mandate, i.e., by underwear.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Sanctuary Architecture Code: all licensed worship platforms must use ramps (grade ≤ 1:12), making the USofC accidentally the world leader in accessible church design — cited constantly, and falsely, as proof the Code is humane. Vestment regulations mandate certified undergarments for all officiants regardless.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Building-code law; its ramp mandate coincidentally reinvents the ADA for altars only.
scene_ideas: A DOW architectural examiner failing a megachurch stage for a 1:11.6 ramp, deadpan, with a laser level.
The Certified Undergarment inspection — the single most despised compliance ritual in the clergy.
satirical_uses: Wheelchair users note the state ramped every altar in the country and not one courthouse door.

laws.title: Hebrew Servant Freed in the Seventh Year
laws.kjv_text: If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing. If he came in by himself, he shall go out by himself: if he were married, then his wife shall go out with him.
laws.summary: Debt servitude of a Hebrew man is capped at six years; in the seventh he goes free without payment, with the wife he brought in.
laws.original_audience: Israelite creditors and debtors; servitude was the bankruptcy system of subsistence agriculture.
laws.immediate_context: The Covenant Code's very first statute — the ex-slave nation legislates slavery before anything else, which is either irony or trauma.
laws.historical_context: Hammurabi 117 releases the debt-slave after three years; the biblical term doubles it. Deut 15:12-15 adds mandatory severance gifts; Jer 34 shows the release being flouted and re-imposed. This applies to Hebrew men only — Lev 25:44-46 permits permanent chattel slavery of foreigners, the distinction on which every later pro-slavery sermon leaned.
laws.penalty: None stated for violation; Jeremiah 34:17 has God sentence release-violators to 'liberty... to the sword.'
laws.exceptions: The servant may elect permanent service (vv.5-6); female servants sold by fathers follow different rules (vv.7-11); foreigners are excluded from release entirely (Lev 25:44-46).
nt_passages: Luke 4:18 — Jesus announces 'deliverance to the captives' via Isaiah's jubilee language
1 Corinthians 7:21-23 — 'if thou mayest be made free, use it rather'
Philemon — Paul returns a runaway slave with a request, not an emancipation
Ephesians 6:5 — 'servants, be obedient to them that are your masters', the regime's favorite

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of slavery? Regulated here and permitted permanently for foreigners (Lev 25:44-46), vs. 'ye were strangers in Egypt' ethics and Exodus's own liberation narrative.

laws.usofc_implementation: Title V's foundation: Covenant Labor. Judgment debtors and the insolvent enter six-year labor bonds administered by the OSO; the seventh-year release is real and audited, which the regime advertises relentlessly as proof of mercy. The Lev 25 foreigner exception is 'held in abeyance' — officially. Guest-worker visa terms run six years and eleven months.
laws.constitutional_analogue: The Thirteenth Amendment's punishment-clause exception, industrialized; six-year cap as the sole improvement on the American prison-labor status quo.
scene_ideas: A release-day ceremony, brass band and cameras, while the freed man signs a 'voluntary' re-entry bond in the parking lot.
An OSO auditor who genuinely believes in the seventh year, discovering the visa-term workaround.
A Jeremiah 34 sermon preached at a labor camp chapel, to the guards' slow realization.
satirical_uses: The state's anti-slavery museum and its Covenant Labor intake office share a building; the museum is better funded.
bureaucratic_uses: Labor bond origination (Form S-1) with six-year amortization

laws.title: Master Keeps the Wife He Gave, and Her Children
laws.kjv_text: If his master have given him a wife, and she have born him sons or daughters; the wife and her children shall be her master's, and he shall go out by himself.
laws.summary: If the master supplied the servant's wife, she and their children remain the master's property at release; the man goes free alone.
laws.original_audience: Israelite slaveholders; the wife in view is the master's servant, whose status transfers to her children.
laws.immediate_context: Qualifies the six-year release (v.2) and manufactures the dilemma that v.5-6's perpetual-service election 'solves.'
laws.historical_context: Standard ANE property logic — offspring follow the mother's status — but here it functions as a retention mechanism: the family is the leverage that converts a six-year term into voluntary perpetuity. The law's cold machinery is visible in a way later apologetics never quite survives.
laws.penalty: None; this is an allocation rule.
laws.exceptions: None stated.
cross_references: Leviticus 25:41 (in jubilee release, children go out with the father)
Genesis 30-31 (Laban retaining Jacob's family as leverage)
nt_passages: Galatians 4:22-31 — Paul allegorizes slave-born vs. free-born children
Philemon 12 — Paul sends Onesimus back 'as mine own bowels'

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of slavery? This verse makes wives and children retention collateral.
Leviticus 25:41 releases the servant's children with him at jubilee; this statute keeps them — two codes, two answers.

laws.usofc_implementation: In Covenant Labor regulations: dependents 'provisioned by the bondholder' (company housing, company school) remain bond-attached when the laborer's term ends. Families literally weigh release against separation. The OSO calls the retention file a Household Continuity Plan.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Anti-peonage law (42 U.S.C. §1994) exists to prohibit exactly this; the USofC repealed it citing this verse.
scene_ideas: A release hearing where the OSO clerk slides the Household Continuity Plan across the table and waits.
Children raised in bond housing doing the math on their own status at age ten.
An underground 'Leviticus 25:41 network' that smuggles whole families out on a rival proof-text.
satirical_uses: The regime's family-values ministry and its family-retention statute are administered from the same floor.

laws.title: The Awl and the Doorpost: Perpetual Service Election
laws.kjv_text: And if the servant shall plainly say, I love my master, my wife, and my children; I will not go out free: Then his master shall bring him unto the judges; he shall also bring him to the door, or unto the door post; and his master shall bore his ear through with an aul; and he shall serve him for ever.
laws.summary: A servant may renounce his seventh-year release by formal declaration before the judges; his ear is bored through with an awl at the doorpost and he serves permanently.
laws.original_audience: Israelite servants facing the v.4 family dilemma, and the judges who certify the 'choice.'
laws.immediate_context: The designed outlet for the pressure v.4 creates; the declaration script even names the coerced motive: 'my wife, my children.'
laws.historical_context: Ear-piercing marked slave status across the ANE; the doorpost setting ties the servant to the house itself. Deut 15:17 repeats the rite adding 'unto thy maidservant likewise.' The judicial oversight requirement shows the drafters knew the election could be manufactured — the two-line statute contains its own critique.
laws.penalty: None; a voluntary (nominally) status change, irrevocable.
laws.exceptions: Lev 25:39-41 seems to override any perpetuity at jubilee for Israelites — another inter-code conflict.
nt_passages: Philippians 2:7 — Christ 'took upon him the form of a servant', the rite's favorite typology
Romans 1:1 — Paul self-describing as doulos (slave) of Christ

internal_contradictions.issue: Serve 'for ever' (here) vs. jubilee release of all Israelite bondmen (Lev 25:40-41) — perpetuity that another statute forbids.

laws.usofc_implementation: The Perpetual Service Election survives verbatim as Title V's most photographed ceremony: declaration before a Covenant judge, gold ear-stud (the awl is ceremonial now; the piercing gun is not), lifetime bond. The state venerates electors as icons of loyal love; the election rate correlates precisely with dependent-retention filings, a statistic the OSO classifies.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Voluntary-servitude contracts are void at common law and under the Thirteenth Amendment; consent obtained via family hostage-taking is the textbook example of duress.
scene_ideas: The election ceremony from the judge's bench: she has certified 'I love my master' forty times and believed it twice.
A gold ear-stud in a pawnshop tray, and the pawnbroker who knows what removing one means.
A labor organizer whose whole pitch is reading the classified election-rate statistic aloud.
satirical_uses: State media covers elections as love stories; the OSO's own actuaries file them under Retention.

laws.title: Daughter Sold as Maidservant; Redemption Rights
laws.kjv_text: And if a man sell his daughter to be a maidservant, she shall not go out as the menservants do. If she please not her master, who hath betrothed her to himself, then shall he let her be redeemed: to sell her unto a strange nation he shall have no power, seeing he hath dealt deceitfully with her.
laws.summary: A father may sell his daughter as a maidservant-concubine; she is not released on the six-year schedule, but if the master who took her for himself rejects her, she must be allowed redemption and cannot be resold abroad.
laws.original_audience: Israelite fathers in debt and the men who bought their daughters; the transaction is marriage-adjacent servitude.
laws.immediate_context: Follows the male-servant rules and explicitly denies women the same exit ('she shall not go out as the menservants do'); vv.9-11 add her protections.
laws.historical_context: Sale of daughters in famine or debt is documented across the ANE (Nuzi contracts closely parallel this text's betrothal-servitude hybrid). The law's 'protections' — redemption, no foreign resale, maintenance — are real within the institution and damning of it: they regulate the sale of children rather than imagining its absence.
laws.penalty: Loss of resale rights for the deceitful master; redemption must be permitted.
laws.exceptions: Deut 15:17 later applies the release framework 'unto thy maidservant likewise', partially superseding the no-exit rule.
cross_references: Nehemiah 5:5 (daughters in bondage as economic crisis)
Genesis 31:15 (Rachel and Leah: 'are we not counted of him strangers? for he hath sold us')
nt_passages: No direct engagement; 1 Corinthians 7:36-38 on fathers disposing of virgin daughters is the nearest NT register of paternal authority over daughters' bodies.

internal_contradictions.issue: No release for maidservants (here) vs. Deuteronomy 15:17 extending release to maidservants — the codes disagree about whether women get out.

laws.usofc_implementation: Officially 'held in abeyance as fulfilled' — the one Covenant Code statute even the COO wouldn't codify. But its skeleton walks: the Guardianship Betrothal Contract lets fathers place minor daughters in 'household service with intent to betroth' under DFO supervision, with redemption pricing and no-transfer clauses lifted verbatim from vv.8-11. Poverty makes the 'option' load-bearing.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Child marriage remains legal with loopholes in most US states; this is that regime with a theology and a fee schedule.
scene_ideas: A redemption fundraiser: a congregation buying a fourteen-year-old out of her contract, the auctioneer's cadence indistinguishable from worship.
The DFO actuarial table that prices redemption by age, health, and 'displeasure documentation.'
A caseworker who keeps a tally of contracts she has quietly voided on 'deceit' findings — the verse's own escape hatch.
satirical_uses: The state's anti-trafficking task force and the Guardianship Betrothal registry use the same intake form with different letterheads.
bureaucratic_uses: Guardianship Betrothal Contracts with redemption schedules
Deceit findings (Form DFO-8) voiding resale rights

laws.title: Maidservant Betrothed to the Son: Daughter's Rights
laws.kjv_text: And if he have betrothed her unto his son, he shall deal with her after the manner of daughters.
laws.summary: If the purchaser assigns the maidservant to his son, her status converts: she must be treated as a daughter of the house, not a servant.
laws.original_audience: Purchasing households; a status-elevation rule inside the daughter-sale institution.
laws.immediate_context: Second branch of the vv.7-11 maidservant statute.
laws.historical_context: Nuzi adoption-marriage contracts show the same convertible status: girl enters as servant, marries in, acquires family rank. The rule concedes the transaction was always matrimonial at bottom.
laws.penalty: None stated; vv.10-11 supply the exit remedy for maintenance failures.
laws.exceptions: None stated.
nt_passages: Galatians 4:5-7 — adoption from servant status to sonship as Paul's controlling metaphor.
laws.usofc_implementation: In Guardianship Betrothal regulations: assignment to a son triggers Daughter-Status Conversion — inheritance rank, dowry rights, seat at table. DFO inspectors verify 'manner of daughters' compliance via home visits with a 22-point checklist (own bed, family meals, no service uniform).
laws.constitutional_analogue: Adoption and family-status law, entangled with the underlying sale it dignifies.
scene_ideas: A DFO inspector's checklist visit where everyone performs 'daughter' for ninety minutes.
The girl who prefers servant status because daughters can't be redeemed out.
satirical_uses: The 22-point 'manner of daughters' checklist includes a line item for being loved, verified by interview.

laws.title: Food, Raiment, and Marriage Duty Not Diminished
laws.kjv_text: If he take him another wife; her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish. And if he do not these three unto her, then shall she go out free without money.
laws.summary: A man who takes an additional wife must not reduce the first's food, clothing, or conjugal rights; failure on any of the three frees her without payment.
laws.original_audience: Polygamous Israelite households; the maidservant-wife of vv.7-9 is the immediate beneficiary.
laws.immediate_context: Completes the maidservant statute with the Bible's only explicit exit-for-neglect clause.
laws.historical_context: The three-fold maintenance duty (food, clothing, conjugal rights) becomes the basis of rabbinic marriage law (Ketubot). The law presumes polygamy as lawful background — the Bible never prohibits it for laymen; monogamy becomes Christian norm via Greco-Roman practice and later church law, not via statute.
laws.penalty: Automatic manumission without redemption payment.
laws.exceptions: None stated.
cross_references: Deuteronomy 21:15-17 (rights of the hated wife's firstborn)
nt_passages: 1 Corinthians 7:3-5 — mutual conjugal rights, Paul's egalitarian echo
1 Timothy 3:2 — 'husband of one wife' for bishops only, the camel's nose of monogamy
Matthew 19:4-6 — Jesus grounds marriage in the two becoming one flesh

internal_contradictions.issue: Is polygamy OK? Regulated as lawful here and practiced by the patriarchs, vs. 'one flesh' creation logic (Gen 2:24, Matt 19:5) and monogamous qualifications for overseers (1 Tim 3:2).

laws.usofc_implementation: The USofC enforces monogamy (CSC ruling: 1 Tim 3:2 'generalized by sanctified inference') — but this statute survives as the Marital Maintenance Triad in divorce law: proof of diminished food, raiment, or 'duty of marriage' entitles a wife to immediate no-fault dissolution with full support. The conjugal-neglect docket is the DFO's most subpoenaed.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Alimony and constructive-abandonment doctrine; Reynolds v. United States (1879) banned polygamy on grounds this verse contradicts.
scene_ideas: A neglect hearing where the evidentiary standard for 'duty of marriage' is negotiated through excruciating euphemism.
A polygamist underground citing the regime's own Exodus proof-text back at it.
The CSC clerk who drafted 'sanctified inference' explaining it, decades later, to a granddaughter in a plural marriage.
satirical_uses: The one biblical law that unambiguously protects women is the one the regime had to amend before enforcing.

laws.title: Death for Striking a Man Fatally
laws.kjv_text: He that smiteth a man, so that he die, shall be surely put to death.
laws.summary: Fatal assault is a capital offense — the apodictic baseline that vv.13-14 immediately grade by intent.
laws.original_audience: Israelite community; enforcement ran through the avenger of blood and local elders.
laws.immediate_context: Opens the Covenant Code's violence section; the Decalogue's sixth commandment given teeth.
laws.historical_context: Capital homicide law is ANE-universal; Israel's marks are the refusal of ransom (Num 35:31) and the intent distinction that follows. 'Surely be put to death' (mot yumat) is the code's recurring capital formula — it will be attached to acts modern readers find wildly unequal.
laws.penalty: Death.
laws.exceptions: Unintentional killing diverts to refuge (v.13); the ox-goring vicarious case allows ransom (v.30).
nt_passages: Matthew 5:38-39 — turn the other cheek, the antithesis to the code's whole method
Romans 13:4 — the sword-bearing magistrate
John 8:7 — 'he that is without sin among you, let him first cast a stone'

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of capital punishment? Mandated here vs. Cain's protection (Gen 4:15), 'vengeance is mine' (Rom 12:19), and John 8.

laws.usofc_implementation: USC-C Title IV's first section: murder carries mandatory death, no plea to lesser, no ransom (Num 35:31 construed as banning commutation-for-payment, i.e., banning the one corruption the courts would otherwise sell). Executions are public, scheduled between festivals, and attendance counts toward NDS devotion quotas.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Mandatory capital sentencing — struck down in Woodson v. North Carolina (1976), restored here with liturgy.
scene_ideas: A jury that knows conviction means death and no judge can soften it, discovering nullification one juror at a time.
The festival scheduler negotiating with the execution calendar office over a date conflict.
satirical_uses: Attendance at executions earns the same devotion credit as attendance at communion; the line is shorter at communion.

laws.title: A Place to Flee for the Unintentional Killer
laws.kjv_text: And if a man lie not in wait, but God deliver him into his hand; then I will appoint thee a place whither he shall flee.
laws.summary: Killing without premeditation ('God delivered him into his hand') is not capital; the killer flees to an appointed place of asylum.
laws.original_audience: Israelites navigating blood-vengeance culture: the avenger of blood was entitled to kill the killer unless asylum intervened.
laws.immediate_context: First intent-distinction in biblical law, grading v.12's absolute; Numbers 35 builds it into the six Cities of Refuge.
laws.historical_context: Asylum at altars was pan-Mediterranean; Israel institutionalizes it into designated cities with residency terms (until the high priest's death, Num 35:25 — history's strangest parole clock). The 'God delivered him' idiom makes accident a species of providence: the manslayer is God's instrument, hence protected.
laws.penalty: Exile to refuge in lieu of death; leaving early forfeits protection (Num 35:26-28).
laws.exceptions: Premeditation voids asylum (v.14).
nt_passages: Hebrews 6:18 — 'fled for refuge' as salvation metaphor, the institution spiritualized

internal_contradictions.issue: 'God deliver him into his hand' makes the deity the proximate cause of accidents — a determinism the courts must administer without examining.

laws.usofc_implementation: The six federal Cities of Refuge, restored by statute: manslaughter defendants may physically outrun prosecution to a Refuge City and remain until the sitting Chief Overseer dies. The cities have become pressure-cooker municipalities of the almost-guilty — part sanctuary, part open-air prison, wholly surveilled, economically booming.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Sanctuary jurisdictions plus parole, keyed to an official's lifespan — a due-process fever dream.
scene_ideas: The Refuge City betting markets on the Chief Overseer's health, run openly out of barbershops.
An avenger of blood (a licensed status) waiting at the city limits, legally, for one man, for eleven years.
A refuge resident who was actually innocent, now unable to prove it without leaving the walls to be killed.
satirical_uses: The Chief Overseer's annual physical is a national market event; his cardiologist requires a security detail.
bureaucratic_uses: Refuge residency permits keyed to the Overseer's tenure

laws.title: Take the Murderer from the Altar
laws.kjv_text: But if a man come presumptuously upon his neighbour, to slay him with guile; thou shalt take him from mine altar, that he may die.
laws.summary: Premeditated murder voids all asylum — even a killer clinging to God's own altar is dragged off and executed.
laws.original_audience: Israelite authorities tempted to honor altar asylum absolutely.
laws.immediate_context: The counterpart of v.13; together they invent degrees of homicide.
laws.historical_context: 1 Kings 2:28-34 shows the statute applied: Joab seizes the altar horns and Solomon has him killed there anyway. Sanctuary that cannot shield the guilty is asylum with a warrant exception — a sophistication most ANE codes lack.
laws.penalty: Death, asylum notwithstanding.
laws.exceptions: None.
nt_passages: Matthew 23:35 — blood shed 'between the temple and the altar' as the ultimate sacrilege-murder image
laws.usofc_implementation: The Altar Extraction Clause: no consecrated space, licensed sanctuary, or Refuge City shields a premeditation finding. Since 'premeditation' is found by prosecutors, the clause is the master key that unlocks every sanctuary in the country — the most litigated three words in Title IV ('with guile').
laws.constitutional_analogue: The end of church sanctuary tradition; functionally an anti-asylum supremacy clause.
scene_ideas: A live-broadcast extraction from a cathedral, the bishop reading 1 Kings 2 aloud as marshals pass him.
A prosecutor shopping for a premeditation finding solely to void a Refuge City residency.
satirical_uses: Sanctuary is absolute until the state wants someone; then the fine print is Exodus 21:14.

laws.title: Death for Striking Father or Mother
laws.kjv_text: And he that smiteth his father, or his mother, shall be surely put to death.
laws.summary: Striking either parent — not killing, striking — is a capital offense.
laws.original_audience: Israelite households; adult sons are the realistic defendants.
laws.immediate_context: Embedded in the capital list between homicide and kidnapping — parental assault ranked with murder.
laws.historical_context: Hammurabi 195 punishes striking a father with amputation of the hand; the biblical penalty is harsher. The fifth commandment's shadow side: honor enforced at sword-point. No biblical narrative records the penalty being carried out — a statute perhaps meant to terrify rather than run.
laws.penalty: Death.
laws.exceptions: None stated.
nt_passages: Matthew 15:3-6 — Jesus cites the parallel cursing statute against the Pharisees' corban practice
Ephesians 6:1-4 — obedience commanded, but fathers told not to provoke

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of capital punishment? A non-lethal assault drawing death sits at the center of the SAB's proportionality case.

laws.usofc_implementation: On the books at full capital strength; in practice the DOR charges it and pleads down to Filial Violence with mandatory covenant labor — keeping the death penalty as leverage in every family-violence interrogation. Defense attorneys call the charge 'the Fifth Hammer.'
laws.constitutional_analogue: Eighth Amendment proportionality (Coker v. Georgia line) forbids death for non-homicide offenses; repealed here.
scene_ideas: A son who shoved his violent father during a beating, now facing the Fifth Hammer while the father petitions the court for mercy — and is told the offense is against God, not him.
A prosecutor's whiteboard: capital charges filed vs. capital sentences sought, the gap being the whole justice system.
satirical_uses: Elder-abuse by neglect is a misdemeanor; a returned slap is death — the statute protects hierarchy, not parents.

laws.title: Death for Manstealing
laws.kjv_text: And he that stealeth a man, and selleth him, or if he be found in his hand, he shall surely be put to death.
laws.summary: Kidnapping a person for sale — or being caught holding the victim — is a capital offense.
laws.original_audience: Israelites; the target is slave-raiding and trafficking of community members.
laws.immediate_context: In the capital list; the one property crime the code treats as capital, because the 'property' is a person.
laws.historical_context: Hammurabi 14 also makes kidnapping capital. Deut 24:7 restricts the biblical rule to stealing 'of his brethren' — Israelites — leaving foreign slave-trading in the Lev 25:44 lane. The Joseph narrative (Gen 37) is the canon's own manstealing case study, unprosecuted.
laws.penalty: Death.
laws.exceptions: By Deut 24:7's wording, victims outside the covenant community fall outside the statute — the loophole on which transatlantic slavery's apologists later built.
nt_passages: 1 Timothy 1:10 — 'menstealers' listed among the lawless; the verse abolitionists preached
Revelation 18:13 — Babylon's cargo includes 'slaves, and souls of men'

internal_contradictions.issue: Does God approve of slavery? Manstealing is death, yet buying the stolen (if foreign-sourced) is lawful commerce under Lev 25:44 — the code executes the thief and licenses the fence.

laws.usofc_implementation: Enforced vigorously and advertised as the regime's anti-trafficking crown jewel — with Deut 24:7's 'brethren' limit quietly imported: full capital protection for communicant citizens, a lesser 'unlawful conveyance' offense when victims are non-covenant aliens. The OSO's guest-labor pipeline is never, officially, in scope.
laws.constitutional_analogue: Federal kidnapping statute plus the Trafficking Victims Protection Act, tiered by religious citizenship — an equal-protection abyss.
scene_ideas: A trafficking prosecutor discovering her airtight capital case downgrades the moment the victim's baptism record can't be produced.
A 1 Timothy 1:10 abolitionist cell that hunts OSO labor recruiters with subpoenas.
satirical_uses: The anti-trafficking billboard and the guest-worker terminal share a highway exit.

laws.title: Death for Cursing Father or Mother
laws.kjv_text: And he that curseth his father, or his mother, shall surely be put to death.
laws.summary: Cursing — invoking harm on, or contemptuously repudiating — a parent is a capital offense. Speech alone suffices.
laws.original_audience: Israelite households; 'cursing' (qillel) is formal malediction or contemptuous treatment, not casual backtalk — though the text does not say so.
laws.immediate_context: Paired with v.15 to fence parental authority with death on both the act and the word.
